feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Europe's climate monitor confirms September was the second-warmest on record globally
entry.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service's September report, published four days late, puts the global average temperature 1.63°C above pre-industrial levels. — Sources: Copernicus Climate Change Service, climate bulletin, 12 October 2026

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany is recovering from its record low, slowly
entry.summary: Germany's main shipping gauge read 17 centimetres on 12 October, up from the record low of minus 6 centimetres set on 1 October. — Sources: Kaub gauge readings, direct fetch via rivercruise.ai, 12 October 2026

entry.title: Singapore recorded its worst air quality of 2026 on 9 October
entry.summary: The 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index in central Singapore climbed to a new 2026 high as haze from Indonesian fires drifted across the region. — Sources: The Star Malaysia, 9 October 2026 · Malay Mail, 9 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fire-hotspot count eased from its 2026 peak but stayed high
entry.summary: The Ministry of Forestry counted 20,818 hotspots nationally on 12 October, down from a 2026 high of 24,952 on 8 October. The count has fallen for several consecutive days from that peak. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Forestry, via databoks.katadata.co.id, 12 October 2026

entry.title: US federal data puts 2024 heat-related worker deaths above the long-run average
entry.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics recorded 48 worker deaths from environmental heat exposure in 2024, above the roughly 42-per-year average across 2011 to 2024. — Sources: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries, 2024 data
